Package org.texttechnologylab.DockerUnifiedUIMAInterface.io.reader.abbyy

Class AbbyyDocumentReader

java.lang.Object
org.apache.uima.resource.Resource_ImplBase
org.apache.uima.resource.ConfigurableResource_ImplBase
org.apache.uima.collection.CollectionReader_ImplBase
org.apache.uima.fit.component.JCasCollectionReader_ImplBase
org.texttechnologylab.DockerUnifiedUIMAInterface.io.reader.abbyy.AbbyyDocumentReader
All Implemented Interfaces:
org.apache.uima.collection.base_cpm.BaseCollectionReader, org.apache.uima.collection.CollectionReader, org.apache.uima.resource.ConfigurableResource, org.apache.uima.resource.Resource
public class AbbyyDocumentReader extends org.apache.uima.fit.component.JCasCollectionReader_ImplBase
Reader class for ABBYY FineReader XMLs. Handles raw or compressed input files (GZip, BZip2, and XZ). Use PARAM_ROOT_PATTERNS to define the root folders of documents within the PARAM_SOURCE_LOCATION, and PARAM_FILE_PATTERNS to filter files within these directories.

The CAS'es produced by this reader will have their DocumentMetaData set according to the root path. You may set the base URI using the PARAM_BASE_URI. It will replace the path prefix above the root path. The documents will have their DocumentId set to the name of their respective root directory. You can als pass a collection ID to be set.

Each element parsed from the ABBYY FineReader files will have some additional metadata set in accordance with the BIOfid project's export structure (which in turn, reflects the Visual Library structure), i.e. the URI of a Page elements will point to $BASE_URI/$PAGE_NAME where the PAGE_NAME is parsed from the file name (e.g. 01_1234567.xml).

    • PARAM_ROOT_PATTERNS

      public static final String PARAM_ROOT_PATTERNS
      A set of Ant-like include/exclude patterns. A pattern starts with [+] if it is an include pattern and with [-] if it is an exclude pattern. The wildcard /**/ can be used to address any number of sub-directories. The wildcard * can be used to a address a part of a name.

      This pattern is used to filter the directories considered document roots. If omitted, will include all directories in the sourceLocation (equvialent to [+]*).

    • PARAM_FILE_PATTERNS

      public static final String PARAM_FILE_PATTERNS
      A set of Ant-like include/exclude patterns. A pattern starts with [+] if it is an include pattern and with [-] if it is an exclude pattern. The wildcard /**/ can be used to address any number of sub-directories. The wildcard * can be used to a address a part of a name.

      This pattern is used to filter the files considered as input. If omitted, will include all XML files in any sub-directory of the sourceLocation (equivalent to [+]**/*.xml*).

    • PARAM_PAGE_ID_PATTERN

      public static final String PARAM_PAGE_ID_PATTERN
      A RegEx pattern string to use on the page file name to determine the page index and ID.

      Use named capturing groups (?<index>) and (?<id>) for page index and ID, respectively. The index will be parsed as an integer while the ID remains unchanged. Defaults to ^\(?<index>d+)_(?<id>\d+).*.

    • PARAM_PRUNE_NESTED_ROOTS

      public static final String PARAM_PRUNE_NESTED_ROOTS
      By default, the AbbyyDocumentReader will not produce multiple CAS'es for nested directories in the PARAM_SOURCE_LOCATION. Instead, the parent root paths will be removed from the list of roots in a post-processing step, after the root path scan. If there are files present in a parent root folder, a warning will be issued and the children will be pruned, instead.
      If this switch is set to false, nested roots will be included which may lead to duplicate document contents!
      See Also:

    • PARAM_BOUNDING_BOX_DEF

      public static final String PARAM_BOUNDING_BOX_DEF
      If given, will only add elements that are fully confined by these relative bounding box coordinates (in domain [0, 100]). Can be an array of one to four values which are interpreted the same way as HTML padding/margin is specified:
      1. {all four sides}
      2. {top/bottom, right/left}
      3. {top, right/left, bottom}
      4. {top, right, bottom, left}

      Example: RelativeBoundingBox.fromString("5,1") -> (5, 99, 95, 1)

      See Also:
